Groves on Making the Bomb

In this account, General Leslie R. Groves describes the challenges of planning amid great uncertainty. In meetings at the University of Chicago in 1942, Groves was taken aback when leading scientists hedged their estimate of how much plutonium was needed for an atomic bomb by a “factor of ten.”
